title: Route 60 to the Master Fund: 7 October and the Plans That Predated It
excerpt: A minute-by-minute account of what failed at the fence on 7 October 2023 — the thin line, the extended rave permit, the Nukhba explosives traced back to unexploded American-made bombs — set against the Gaza reconstruction plans, Peace to Prosperity through Project Sunrise, that priced the coastline years before the war that cleared it.
content:
Thursday afternoon on Route 60 through Huwara. A man walks up to an Israeli car in traffic and empties a pistol into it. Pregnant woman at the wheel. A year-and-a-half-old in the back. They drive. Hours later a Haruv team finds him and shoots him dead. The gun is on him.

That is 5 October 2023. An average problem on that road. Huwara is the pipe. Settlers drive it every day through a Palestinian town that has already been burned once, in February, after two brothers were killed nearby. The army treats the stretch as a standing requirement. Guards exist because the road is an argument that uses live ammunition.

Friday the settlers put up a tent in the same town, prayed, marched, smashed shops and cars. Labib Dumaidi, nineteen, a student, died. His family told Yesh Din he was on the roof trying to keep rocks off the house when he was shot in the chest. The army said its own men fired at someone throwing a brick at an Israeli vehicle and that it did not know of a settler discharging a weapon. Fifty-one people were wounded at the funeral. Three of them by live fire. No journalist. No American passport. A student and a road.

Kan later reported that two companies from the Commando Brigade, about a hundred soldiers who had been sitting as backup on the Gaza line through the holidays, were sent to Huwara after the Thursday shooting. Daniel Hagari said the standing numbers on the fence itself had not changed. Those companies were reinforcement, not the line. He also said the move would be investigated. Roy Sharon wrote that, as far as he could tell, nobody replaced them.

Two days later the fence came down.

On 21 May 2025 Benjamin Netanyahu stood up and priced that morning. Sandals. AK-47s. Pickup trucks. Cheap, he said. The Qatari money that crossed into Gaza for years on Shin Bet and Mossad recommendation did not buy 7 October because 7 October did not require F-35s. He called Qatargate a libel. He said he knew nothing about Jonatan Urich and Eli Feldstein taking Qatari money to polish Doha. Qatar is not a friendly state. He would let a law calling it an enemy go through. Contact for the hostages would have to stay legal.

Then he asked how there was no one next to the fence. How there was a directive not to be next to the fence. How the Air Force received orders only hours after the attack. How did it happen. He named one place the directive was not given. Ein HaShlosha. Nothing happened there, he said. The community was not invaded. The men who came were killed. He said he lets the public decide every day. Elections when they come.

The IDF's own later count put 767 troops on the whole Gaza line at first light, facing more than five thousand men coming the other way. Holiday weekend. Simchat Torah. Gaza Division officers, when they first saw the request to keep a rave going through Saturday, said the line was already halved for the holiday and they did not have the men.

Unity had been permitted for the night of 5–6 October. On 2 October the producers asked to keep the same field, the same kit, through Saturday for a second party called Nova. Lt. Col. Fogel in the Gaza Division said no. Needless risk west of Route 232. Brig. Gen. Avi Rosenfeld and Col. Haim Cohen said the same thing that week. Do not add three thousand civilians at dawn. Col. Nimrod Cibolski in the Operations Division told Fogel on the phone to approve the extension. Cohen's name went on the permit. Nova was still running at 6:29. Music first. Then rockets. Then the exits.

Golani's 13th Battalion held the Nahal Oz sector. The battalion commander, Lt. Col. Tomer Greenberg, was at home in Kibbutz Almog on the Dead Sea. He got the rocket call at 6:30 and drove. His deputy was already on the net. Ynet's later probe names him Major N., deputy commander of the 13th, the man telling all stations at 6:31 that this was a complex event, purple rain and Turkish cavalry, and then watching from an observation post as a breach dumped men onto the road toward Sa'ad junction. Soldiers from the mortar platoon later said they had been told the night before there would be a Saturday morning drill. Some were still in sleepwear when the first barrage hit. Men described fighting two or three hundred meters from the wire without vests. Jerusalem to that fence is about forty-five minutes in a helicopter. The lag before a coherent answer reached the perimeter has been given as six hours.

Raviv Drucker and others published the other room. Brig. Gen. Ido Mizrahi, appointed by Chief of Staff Herzi Halevi to run the army's inquiry into Nova, sat with Southern District police commander Amir Cohen and Cohen's officers. Hasson reported the tape. Mizrahi told them, for the first time they were hearing it, that on the night of 6–7 October Halevi, Shin Bet chief Ronen Bar, Southern Command's Yaron Finkelman, and Operations Directorate chief Oded Basiuk held consults at midnight and again around 4 a.m. Signs. They assessed routine. They set another meeting for 8 a.m. The breach was at 6:30. Cohen's people said if that 4 a.m. picture had reached the district, the festival would have been emptied. Southern District had been the ones who, at 6:30, called it an invasion and started pushing people off the field. The army was not there yet.

The yard of cars is the other inventory. Aerials of it went around the world in the first week. Burned roofs collapsed into cabins. No glass. A yellow loader at the edge. About 860 wrecks came off Route 232 and the festival ground to a wheat field at Tkuma. Four hundred were cleared to drive again. Two hundred eighty were burned past recognition. Some had been shot through the engine block and then the cabin. Some had taken anti-tank rounds. Some had tank tracks over them.

In November 2023 the Rabbanut approved burying cars because the blood and tissue could not be taken out of the steel. ZAKA and the rabbinate said so together. Police later pulled possible bone from two of the hulls that had taken AT missiles. An Israel Antiquities Authority team walking 232 near the Mefalsim bend found a woman's remains melted into the asphalt, a necklace and hair still there.

A fragmentation grenade does not do that. An anti-tank warhead does. A thermobaric charge does. A cabin full of gasoline does. AKs punch holes. Netanyahu priced the holes.

The Nukhba force was built as the cross-border raid arm of the Qassam Brigades. Close work. Fence, outpost, kibbutz, festival ground. Ra'ad Sa'ad, while operations chief, established those battalions, per the IDF's own December 2025 kill notice. Ayman Nofal sat on the general military council, ran the central Gaza brigade and air operations, and, the IDF said, had the Nukhba picture at Be'eri and at Re'im. Asharq Al-Awsat, citing people around Qassam, put Nofal in the five-man planning cell with Yahya Sinwar, Mohammed Deif, Mohammed Sinwar, and Rouhi Mushtaha. Nofal was killed in an airstrike on 17 October 2023. Sa'ad lived until 13 December 2025. After Sinwar pulled him off operations in 2021 he ran weapons production. Netanyahu and Israel Katz put their names on the announcement that he was dead and called him one of the architects. Hamas confirmed it the next day.

What crossed with them included thermobaric grenades and RPG warheads. The New York Times, from remnants and Israeli officials, put those in the kit. A UK parliamentary commission on 7 October wrote that thermobaric grenades and RPGs were used against houses in Be'eri and Kfar Aza and against civilian cars, and that the open literature puts the burn near 3,000 degrees Celsius. Identification of some of the dead took weeks. Propane and gasoline from the houses were used as accelerant after. If Sa'ad and Nofal built the force that ran that kit, the force is not a pair of sandals.

Some of the fill in those charges did not start in a workshop in Gaza. It started in a bomb that did not go off.

After 2014 the Qassam engineering teams were told, on camera to Al Jazeera in 2020, to collect the unexploded howitzer rounds and the American MK-84s and turn the crisis into stock. Michael Cardash, former deputy of Israeli police bomb disposal, told the New York Times in January 2024 that unexploded Israeli-launched ordnance is a main source of Hamas explosive. They cut the cases open and take the filler. A Western official in the same piece said most of the explosive Hamas was using in the war looked like it had been cooked out of those duds. A 750-pound body that fails is hundreds of rockets. An MK-84 that fails is roughly half a ton of Tritonal still sitting in the steel.

The Open Source Munitions Portal has the photograph of the method. An MK-84 with the fuze and the baseplate off. The retaining ring on a sheet. The filler gone. That is the harvest. Bellingcat, reading a dud MK-84 that came down in Sanaa, traced a lot number to General Dynamics Tactical Systems, United States, 2017. Same family of body Israel drops on Gaza. GBU-39s are not made in Israel. They are made here. Woodward in Colorado stamps CAGE 81873 on parts. The Times found that code on fragments in Rafah. Bellingcat later found three GBU-39 tails in al-Tuffah, one of them a dud. Boeing makes the JDAM kit that turns the dumb MK-84 into a guided one. Brian Castner found JDAM scrap in Gaza after 2021. The kit can fail and leave the bomb intact. The bomb can fail and leave the kit.

Haaretz and TheMarker, May 2025: the Air Force itself counted at least three thousand duds in Gaza by early 2025. UNMAS puts failure across the campaign at five to ten percent. After stocks of good fuzes ran out, the IAF fitted older ones, some of them American-supplied, some decades old. Dud rates that used to sit near two percent jumped, in some lots, toward twenty. Tens of millions of dollars of explosive, sitting in the rubble, already paid for once.

You will not get a serial off a thermobaric grenade from 7 October that still says Dayton or McAlester or General Dynamics. The fill does not keep the stencil. What you get is the body they opened, the contractor mark on the tail that did not fire, and Qassam saying out loud in 2020 that the MK-84 was part of the diet. American soil and American shifts made the case and the Tritonal. Israeli aircraft delivered it. The fuze quit. Someone with a saw finished the job.

Some of the fire on the roads is not theirs. Haaretz, from documents and testimony, reported that officers in the Gaza Division put the Hannibal procedure in force that morning at Erez, at Re'im, and at the Nahal Oz outpost. The written directive had been withdrawn in 2016. The logic that circulated was the old one. Stop a capture even if it means hitting the people being taken. Shortly before 11:30 Southern Command put out that no vehicle was to go back into Gaza. A Southern Command source told the paper everyone understood those vehicles could be carrying kidnapped civilians or soldiers.

Channel 12 and an IAF probe put Efrat Katz, 68, of Nir Oz, in a car a combat helicopter fired on. The army's own inquiry said she was likely killed by that fire. At Be'eri, Brig. Gen. Barak Hiram, 99th Division, ordered a tank to put shells into a house where Hamas men were holding Israelis. He told the New York Times the order was to break in even at the cost of civilian casualties. Yasmin Porat and Hadas Dagan walked out of that house. A tank crew later said they had applied Hannibal to a vehicle they believed was carrying abducted soldiers.

An overhead of the salvage lot does not sort which hull is which fire.

The document Israel called Jericho Wall, about forty pages, was in Israeli hands more than a year out. The New York Times published the contents in November 2023 from officials who had seen it. Rocket barrage at the start. Drones against the cameras and the remote machine guns on the towers. Men across the fence on foot, motorcycles, paragliders. The Washington Post, from footage posted as it happened, described the morning itself. Snipers and explosive drones taking out the watchtowers that held the cameras, the thermal imagers, the radar. Once those were down the Nukhba columns moved. That is the source for the drones-on-cameras line. It is in the captured plan and it is in the video from 6:30.

The spotters, the tatzpitaniyot, said afterward they had been watching the rehearsals for months. Crashing the fence. Taking hostages. The warnings went up and came back down.

July 2023. A veteran 8200 analyst wrote that a daylong Hamas exercise matched Jericho Wall, including the Quran line printed at the top of the plan. Encrypted mail viewed by the Times. A colonel in the Gaza division called the scenario imaginary. Wait patiently. She wrote back that she utterly refuted that it was imaginary. In September another 8200 NCO, Channel 12 called her Vav, sent the Ezekiel line. The sword is coming. Warn the nation. A colonel ordered a successor's briefing to Halevi rewritten so Jericho Wall would not appear in it.

Gallant called them human animals on 9 October when he announced the siege. Sa'ad still built a force. Nofal still ran air and the central brigade. The 8200 women still watched the rehearsals. Hiram still gave a tank order. Halevi and Bar still set the next meeting for 8 a.m. The speech and the competence do not cancel.

The cheap sentence is sandals and AKs. The fill in some of the charges that cooked the cars came out of metal that failed the first time it was dropped. Some of that metal was poured in the United States.

The Qatari cash is a separate machine that ran at the same time as the thin line and the extra day. Netanyahu said the purpose out loud long before the May presser. Keep Hamas in Gaza and the Palestinian Authority in the West Bank as separate governments. Division as policy. The suitcases had a job when they crossed. In May he added that the transfer was recommended by Shin Bet and Mossad, then separated that money from the massacre by pricing the visible kit. Both sentences are his.

January 2020. Peace to Prosperity. One hundred eighty-one pages on the White House site. This document is about Gaza. Section Nine is titled Gaza Criteria. Israel implements its side only if a body acceptable to Israel has full control of Gaza, the organizations there are disarmed, and Gaza is demilitarized.

Page 37: the agreement leads to the dismantling of all Palestinian refugee camps and the building of permanent housing.

Page 19: more than forty kilometers of coastline that could develop into a modern metropolitan city overlooking the beach. Comparables printed the way an offering memorandum prints comparables. Beirut, Hong Kong, Lisbon, Rio de Janeiro, Singapore, Tel Aviv. An artificial island for a port, subject to Israel's security and environmental requirements. Gaza Marine at 1.5 trillion cubic feet.

More than $50 billion over ten years. Page 19. Page 57. Page 137.

Page 61 names the vehicle. Peace to Prosperity Master Fund. Not a framework. A fund. With Master in the name.

When that paper landed the press treated it as a joke because none of the ground existed. Hamas ran Gaza. The camps were cities of concrete. Neighborhoods sat on the water. The document already knew the donor problem. International money would not keep arriving, it said, so long as the governing structure provoked confrontations that destroyed the last round of investment. New money waited on a different government.

The analysts who called it dead on arrival ran the logic correctly and pointed it the wrong way. You could not get those preconditions by talking. They read the war as the obstacle.

UNOSAT's October 2025 composite, damage assessment 35851, put about 81 percent of structures in the damaged-or-destroyed column. Roughly 198,273 buildings. Municipal archives and a central registry office were among the buildings that did not survive. Deeds. Titles. Who owned the plot.

Page 37 wanted the camps dismantled and permanent housing built. A population with somewhere else to go can refuse the new housing. A population on the rubble of its own plot cannot.

February 15, 2024. Kushner with Tarek Masoud at Harvard, Middle East Initiative. The tape is on the program channel.

Gaza's waterfront property, it could be very valuable, if people would focus on building up livelihoods.

Then: it's a little bit of an unfortunate situation there, but I think from Israel's perspective I would do my best to move the people out and then clean it up.

He added that he did not think Israel had said they could not come back. On the same tape: if he were running Israel he would bulldoze something in the Negev, move civilians there, and finish the job. When the clip moved he posted the full exchange and said Palestinian lives improve only when their leadership is held to account.

October 19, 2025. 60 Minutes. Five years and nine months after Peace to Prosperity went up on the White House site. Two years and twelve days after 7 October. Ceasefire days old. Bodies still coming out of the rubble in the same hour Steve Witkoff says they are already talking to contractors from all of the Middle Eastern countries.

Lesley Stahl asks who awards the contracts. A board of peace, he says. Fastidious about talent. Everything's transparent that we do. Yes.

Then the number. The estimates are in the $50 billion range.

Then: a group of people working on master plans for the last two years. That is, since the autumn of 2023.

Stahl: so there are plans already.

Witkoff: we have plans already. We have a master plan already.

Kushner, eleven seconds later: yeah. So, so basically over the last couple years there's been a lot of organizations that have been trying to determine what happens after the war.

Master plan becomes organizations. Fifty billion is the number printed three times in the 2020 paper. You can believe a reconstruction estimate and a prospectus independently landed on the same round number. You can also notice the word.

Kushner had already flown in, before the hostages were out, looked at the ground, and told Stahl it looked like a nuclear bomb had been set off. He asked the IDF where the people walking north were going. They said back to the plot, to pitch a tent. He said it was very sad. They really have nowhere else to go. The sentence is true. It is also page 37 spoken as weather.

December 2025. The Wall Street Journal gets a 32-slide deck, sensitive but unclassified. Project Sunrise. Building a New and Unified Gaza. Team led by Kushner and Witkoff, Josh Gruenbaum from the White House, about forty-five days of work, input from Israeli officials and contractors.

Cost slide: $112.1 billion over ten years. Housing the largest line, $36.1 billion. United States as anchor, nearly $60 billion in grants and debt guarantees in the draft the Journal saw. The administration later called the U.S.-pays reading fake news.

Slide 2, per the reporting, says the rest does not move unless Hamas is disarmed. That is Section Nine of the 2020 paper with a new cover.

A slide titles rebuilt Rafah as seat of governance. More than 100,000 housing units. Two hundred-plus schools. Seventy-five-plus medical sites. Another slide talks about monetizing 70 percent of the coastline beginning in year ten and puts long-run return on that coast above $55 billion. The deck does not say where two million people live while the rubble is cleared.

Marc Rowan later put his own numbers on the same coast. Those are his numbers. They sit in the file with Kushner's February sentence and with page 19.

The Board of Peace is a different document from Peace to Prosperity. Peace to Prosperity is the 2020 White House paper and it is about Gaza on almost every economic page. The Board of Peace charter, written after UN Security Council resolution 2803, is the body Witkoff pointed to when Stahl asked who awards the contracts. That charter, in the version European Council on Foreign Relations and others described after Davos, does not mention Gaza. It talks about replacing institutions that have failed.

Trump permanent chairman. He picks the members. Simple majority plus the chairman. A billion dollars for a permanent seat in the version that circulated. Twenty-one countries in at Davos. Most of Europe stayed out. Netanyahu was not in the room. ICC warrant. The Arabic on the New Gaza renderings had spelling mistakes.

The 2020 donor sentence is still the sentence under the checks. Money will not go into a structure that will be knocked down again. Governance first. Disarmament as the condition of the transfer. Slide 2 of Sunrise says the same thing Section Nine said when the camps were still standing and the joke was that the paper was dead.

The paper did not need a date. It needed the city it treated as an obstacle to stop being the city in the way.

Netanyahu's May inventory and the salvage yard cannot both be the whole morning. The prospectus and the leveled registry cannot both be a coincidence of vocabulary.

Yoav Gallant. Ra'ad Sa'ad. Ayman Nofal. Yahya Sinwar. Mohammed Deif. Tomer Greenberg. Major N. Ido Mizrahi. Amir Cohen. Herzi Halevi. Ronen Bar. Yaron Finkelman. Oded Basiuk. Vav. Barak Hiram. Efrat Katz. Yasmin Porat. Hadas Dagan. Labib Dumaidi. Lt. Col. Fogel. Nimrod Cibolski. Haim Cohen. Avi Rosenfeld. Michael Cardash. Jared Kushner. Tarek Masoud. Steve Witkoff. Lesley Stahl. Josh Gruenbaum. Marc Rowan. Jonatan Urich. Eli Feldstein. Benjamin Netanyahu. Israel Katz.

location.name: The Gaza perimeter fence, Route 232 — Re'im, Nahal Oz, and Huwara
